brief.offer: Video case studies with engineering teams that use your product

facts.claim: Tuple makes a remote pair-programming app for macOS and Windows, designed for developers.
facts.excerpt: The best remote pair programming app on macOS and Windows

facts.claim: The app supports full-time mouse and keyboard control for both participants, along with command-line integration and pluginability.
facts.excerpt: Seamless collaboration with full-time mouse and keyboard support for both parties, snappy interactions, command-line integration and pluginability.

facts.claim: Tuple integrates with Slack, letting users start pairing sessions from a channel or direct message and join with one click.
facts.excerpt: adds a `/tuple` command, which will start a pairing session directly from a channel or DMs. Anyone can then join your call with a single click

research.website_note: The results identify tuple.app as Tuple’s official site and link it to the Tuple company profile and product.
research.gaps: No current pricing, customer names, recent launches, funding, or stated business priorities are provided.

dropped.claim: Tuple has 13 employees listed on LinkedIn.

strategy.observation: Tuple’s Slack integration lets users start pairing sessions from a channel or direct message and join with one click.
strategy.offer_link: A video case study could follow an engineering team from a Slack discussion into a Tuple pairing session, showing prospective customers how the integration fits into real development work rather than just demonstrating the feature.
hypotheses: Engineering prospects may find a real team's workflow more persuasive than a standalone integration demo.
The Head of Marketing may want customer-led content that makes Tuple’s day-to-day use concrete.
strategy.angle: Would a video case study following an engineering team from a Slack discussion into a Tuple pairing session be useful for your marketing?
strategy.fit_reason: The offer provides a concrete way to show an existing Tuple workflow through customer experience, although demand for video case studies and access to willing customers are unconfirmed.

draft.subject: Slack flow case study
draft.body:
Tuple’s Slack flow seems easier to show in a real team workflow than in a feature demo.

I make short video case studies with engineering teams that use the product. My guess is a story that follows a Slack discussion into a Tuple pairing session would make the day-to-day use feel concrete for prospects.

Would you be open to testing that format with one customer?
